channel.title: HPCC Service Status
channel.description: We'll post information about ICER's system downtimes, updates, new features, and other information for the ICER user community here.

item.title: Rolling Reboots
item.description: ICER will be conducting rolling patches and reboots of gateway, development, and compute nodes starting Monday, October 26, 2026. These rolling reboots may impact access to individual gateway/development nodes and increase queue times as individual nodes are scheduled for reboot as this will reduce the total number of nodes available for running jobs. This process will not affect running jobs on the compute nodes, but open sessions on gateways and development nodes will be closed when rebooted. We will post updates to this blog when the process is complete.

item.title: ICER/HPCC Access and MSU Password Reset Information
item.description:
ICER/HPCC Access and MSU Password Reset Information

The University is requiring a password reset for all accounts accessing MSU systems. If you are having issues accessing ICER/HPCC when using a password to authenticate and have not changed it recently, you will need to reset your password by visiting https://auth.msu.edu and following the procedure presented for your NetID. For those users with an FPID account, if you have issues resetting your password through https://auth.msu.edu, you may need to reactivate your FPID using your PIN, which will reset your password. The MSU IT password management help page is here: https://netid.msu.edu/password/index.html, they would be able to assist with any password reset issues.

HPCC Staff

item.title: Research Storage: IO Errors - UPDATED 10/27/26
item.description:
UPDATE: 10/27/26 - The failing hardware has been replaced successfully. We are continuing to troubleshoot the IO error root cause with our storage vendor.

UPDATE: 10/26/26 - A failing hardware component has been identified within the research filesystem while troubleshooting the reported IO errors. That component is scheduled to be replaced by our storage vendor the morning of Tuesday, October 27, 2026. No impact to users or workflows is anticipated, and this blog will be updated as soon as the new hardware is installed.

Following the power outage, ICER is aware of some users seeing IO errors when accessing some files on the research filesystem. We are actively working with our storage vendor to resolve these errors, and will provide an update as soon as we are able.

item.title: Scratch Storage: Intermittent Write Errors
item.description:
Scratch Storage: Intermittent Write Errors

We are investigating intermittent write errors affecting scratch storage. Users may encounter errors when jobs or other processes attempt to write files to scratch.

Our team is addressing storage utilization issues we believe to be the cause at this time.

item.title: Home Filesystem Currently Offline - RESOLVED
item.description:
RESOLVED: 3:45PM The home file system has been restored and the scheduler has been resumed.

The VAST home filesystem is currently offline. The scheduler is currently paused while we address this issue. OnDemand web sessions may be inaccessible as well. We are currently working with our software vendor to bring the home filesystem back online.

item.title: Home Filesystem SMB Currently Offline - RESOLVED
item.description:
SMB access to the home filesystem has been restored.

Due to a system issue, SMB access to the home filesystem is currently offline. We’ll update this blog post when SMB access is available.

item.title: MSU Network Errors - RESOLVED
item.description:
RESOLVED: ICER has recovered from the power outage and all systems should be online and accessible.

UPDATE: 4:30pm 9/21/2026
The cluster is up and healthy. Some hardware from the outage will require more attention but most everything is up.
Please contact us if you notice anything wrong.

UPDATE: 3:20pm 9/21/2026
The amd24 cluster is available now

UPDATE: 3:00pm 9/21/2026
The amd20 cluster is available now

UPDATE: 1:30pm 9/21/2026
The intel18 cluster is available now

UPDATE: 11:30am 9/21/2026
Gateways, OpenOnDemand, and Globus access are enabled. Dev nodes are up. Usage should be back to normal on those. Continuing with the remaining cluster nodes.

UPDATE: 10:00am 9/21/2026
MSU Power is now stable and ICER can begin the process of returning to normal. We are currently in maintenance mode to test critical functions. User access is blocked during testing. Once we confirm internal stability, we will return the cluster back to production in sections starting with dev nodes. We will provide updates as this happens.

UPDATE: 10:30am 9/20/2026
As many of you know, the university experienced a widespread power outage that began last night. While power has largely been restored, there are significant ongoing challenges and ICER’s computing systems have been shut down in order to reduce power consumption and to avoid damaging equipment. We will resume normal operations as soon as possible; however, it is likely that this will not be until at least tomorrow (Monday, 9/21).

ICER is experiencing random errors due to a larger MSU Network Issue. We will continue monitoring the situation when the campus wired network is stable again.

item.title: Home Filesystem Maintenance Friday 09/18/26 - RESOLVED
item.description:
RESOLVED - The home filesystem maintenance is complete.

UPDATE - 10/27/26 - Our planned maintenance is complete. However, during maintenance a hardware component failed in the home filesystem cluster, and we are working with our vendor to replace this component as quickly as possible. There is no anticipated impact to users or workflows, and this blog post will be updated as soon as the hardware is replaced.

UPDATE - 10/15/26 - Home filesystem maintenance will continue Friday, 10/16/26, at 6AM. Following the 10/16/26 maintenance, one more maintenance task will be completed the week of 10/19/26. This blog will be updated again once all home filesystem maintenance is complete.

UPDATE - 9/23/26 - Some of the home filesystem maintenance was postponed and is scheduled to be completed the week of 9/28/26. This blog will be updated when the maintenance is complete.

On Friday, September 18th, a minor configuration change will be applied to the home file system. No outage or performance impacts are anticipated. This blog will be updated once the configuration change is complete.

item.title: Scavenger Queue Paused - UPDATED 10/21
item.description:
UPDATE: 10/21: Our software vendor has reproduced the issue and developed a patch. We will apply this patch once we complete internal testing.

UPDATE: 10/7: Some other types of job requests were found to still trigger this preemption issue. We have implemented a workaround to ensure scavenger jobs are preempted properly while we work with our software vendor to address the underlying issue.

RESOLVED: 9/22: The scavenger queue is back online. We identified the job requests that trigger the preemption issue and implemented scheduler logic to account for them.

UPDATE: 9/18: We are working with our software vendor to resolve this issue.

We have temporarily paused running jobs through the scavenger queue while we investigate a potential issue with job preemption. If you have any questions, please contact us.

item.title: Nodes down - RESOLVED 8/26
item.description:
RESOLVED - All nodes affected during maintenance are back into service. Some nodes in the HPCC are still offline, but this is due to typical hardware issues and is in line with usual compute node availability.

After yesterday’s maintenance, some compute nodes are not available for job scheduling. This is primarily affecting nodes with GPUs. Jobs requesting GPUs will likely queue for longer than usual or, depending on constraints, will stay in the queue until nodes are returned to service.

Our system administrators are working on this and will return nodes to service as soon as possible. Updates will be posted here.
